# Save corpus

Real saves from the phone playthrough (`npm run e2e:season`), one file per save
version at each point: `v<version>-<point>.json`, about 120 KB each.
Before format 24, `tests/qa/corpus.test.ts` checked that every save migrated to `SAVE_VERSION`,
passed the soak's invariant checks and played on headless: a whole season for the
oldest and the newest version here, past the season's end for the `mid-season` save of one version in between, four weeks for the rest (a season
each made the corpus the slowest file in CI's 10-minute check job).

Rules:

- **Never edit a file here.** Each one is what a player on that version has in
  their phone; format 24 must reject older versions and keep their data intact.
- **Add, don't replace.** When `SAVE_VERSION` moves, run the playthrough on the new
  `main` and copy its `after-tutorial`, `mid-season`, `after-rollover` and `live-rivals`
  dumps from `e2e-output/<WxH>/saves/` here (the file names already carry the version).
  Old versions stay. The soak's old-save runs don't read these files: they build each old
  version from a fresh game (`asOldSave`); only `tests/qa/corpus.test.ts` plays them.

Points the playthrough dumps: `after-tutorial` (new game, nothing advanced yet),
`mid-season` (facilities, a signing, a kit, event cards answered, about round 14),
`after-rollover` (season 2, week 1: history, aged squad, juniors, new fixtures),
`season-2` (a week into season 2) and, from v13, `live-rivals` (the held-week step: rival
matches on the match engine turned on and one round of them played).

Format 24 (#536) is new careers only: historical fixtures remain immutable and
now assert friendly rejection with untouched source data. The v24 after-tutorial
fixture is generated by `createNewGame` plus `initLeague` (seed 536, openAll);
it validates and plays a full season in the corpus test.

Format 25 (#570) preserves supported v24 careers through a metadata-only migration;
it never converts a legacy league into a pyramid. The three new v25 fixtures are
generated source regressions (seed 570, `createNewGame` and `initLeague`), not phone
playtest evidence: AU after-tutorial, UK after-tutorial, and dormant AU competition
metadata. The metadata snapshot includes rules/prizes, explicit identity and a
scheduled test tie; the existing gameplay path intentionally ignores it until the
later calendar issue activates competition careers. Historical files stay intact.

Format 26 (#571) adds an explicit isolated developer calendar. The three v26
fixtures are generated from source with seed 571 using the same AU, UK and
dormant-metadata cases as v25. They exercise supported legacy careers through
the new migration; structural active/held/rollover saves have focused source
regressions in `tests/systems/competitionCalendar.test.ts`. These are not phone
playtest evidence, and no production competition entry is activated.
